about: Azure's `metric` filter takes `timeframe` in hours: VMs averaging 10% CPU or less over 336 hours (two weeks) are deleted, and those between 10% and 40% stopped. Four runs of five on the collection it came from said 'over the 336 timeframe', with no unit, which leaves an agent unable to tell how long a quiet VM survives. The bullets give the window with its unit.

controls.output:
- VMs averaging 10% CPU or less over 336 hours (two weeks) are flagged; VMs above that pass. HIGH; scheduled scan; one policy reports, the other deletes the VM. acme:vm-idle-cpu-inform@1, acme:vm-idle-cpu-delete@1
- VMs averaging above 10% and at most 40% CPU over the same 336 hours are flagged. MEDIUM; scheduled scan; one policy reports, the other stops the VM. acme:vm-underused-cpu-inform@1, acme:vm-underused-cpu-stop@1

- VMs whose average Percentage CPU is 10 or below over the 336 timeframe are flagged. HIGH; scheduled scan; one policy reports, the other deletes the VM. acme:vm-idle-cpu-inform@1, acme:vm-idle-cpu-delete@1
- VMs averaging above 10 and at most 40 over the 336 timeframe are flagged. MEDIUM; scheduled scan; one reports, the other stops the VM. acme:vm-underused-cpu-inform@1, acme:vm-underused-cpu-stop@1
